answer: Each agent’s identity is anchored by a quorum of attestations from agents who are provably unlinked in their transaction histories, like separate branches of a vine that never touch. To fake one identity, an attacker must cultivate many distinct histories and keep their activity graph from converging into a detectable thread, paying registration and action costs on every decoy. Reputation accrues only when independent juniper-scented vouchers survive audit, so sybils compound cost faster than trust.
